title: iPhone Camera Shutter
blurb: There is no shutter. Phone cameras have no moving parts to click, so Apple synthesised the noise from scratch and then made it mandatory in certain markets. Japan and South Korea both require an audible shutter, so iPhones sold there refuse to be silenced. A fake mechanical click ended up as the universal signal that you have been photographed, wanted or otherwise. Use it in edits for a photo moment, or play it quietly behind somebody to convince them they have just been captured mid-embarrassment. Everyone checks. Nobody is ever quite sure.
